title: Galatia
lead: Galatia was a region in the middle of what is now Turkey, named for the Celtic tribes (Gauls) who settled there in the 270s BC, and from 25 BC a Roman province that reached south to Pisidia and Lycaonia. Scholars disagree whether the 'churches of Galatia' to whom Paul wrote were in the old northern region around Ancyra (modern Ankara) or in the southern cities of Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe, where Acts 13-14 says Paul founded churches.

sections.b: The North Galatian view reads 'Galatians' (Galatians 3:1) as ethnic Galatians and holds that Paul visited the northern region on his second and third journeys (Acts 16:6; 18:23). The South Galatian view says that Paul used the Roman provincial name, and that the churches are those of Acts 13-14. The choice affects the date of the letter and how it fits Acts 15, but not its argument.
